concept: Accordion prints every section of a unit as a line of the case, like a legend: the sections that are open are lit with an ink index bar and a minus, the ones that wait stay in plain sight with a plus, and nobody has to open a menu to learn what the unit holds.

default_to_avoid.pattern: accordion of bordered cards, each header a full-width bar with a rotating chevron and a tinted fill on the open one
default_to_avoid.why_not: Boxed bars read as a stack of buttons or input fields, and a tint tells open from closed by colour alone; dial prints a legend instead.

default_to_avoid.pattern: accordion that jumps open with a spring bounce on every header press
default_to_avoid.why_not: Only the loud control may carry a settle, and a section is plain printing, so it opens on the state motion tokens and nothing overshoots.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): band names printed in a column on the case, the tuned one marked beside its name
system/CONCEPT.md P7 The legend is the state: every choice printed, the one in use lit

derivation.consequence: a legend is printing, never a key
derivation.form: The header is a printed word with no fill, no border and no raised edge, so only the open one carries a short ink index bar beside it.

derivation.consequence: and the chosen one turns medium
derivation.form: A closed title prints in regular weight and secondary ink and an open one turns medium in primary ink, so state shows in the type itself.

derivation.consequence: in one fixed column or arc, so the lit word moves and nothing reflows
derivation.form: Every title sits on one left edge, and an open section's content stands under its title on the same edge with a seam between sections.

derivation.consequence: Home and End reach the ends, Space and Enter press
derivation.form: Up and Down step between headers, Home and End reach the first and last, and Space or Enter opens or closes the focused one.

derivation.consequence: fast in, slow out, through the state motion tokens
derivation.form: A section opens on motion.enter and closes on motion.exit, and the panel stays mounted until its leave has finished.

options.name: legend lines with an index bar

variants.reason: A follows P7: the sections are printing and the open one is lit by an index bar, a minus and weight. B cuts each section as a window, which is the Input well, so a header looks editable. C makes every header a raised key, which turns a list of sections into a row of loud parts.

root.why: One column of sections that fills its container, so every title sits on the same edge and the list does not shift sideways when a section opens.

item.why: One section holds its header and panel and is parted from the next by a seam, a 1px divider line, never a box, so the legend stays printing.

heading.why: The heading element gives screen reader users the list of sections, and it carries no style of its own so the type sizes come from the trigger.

trigger.why: The whole header row is one 44px target with the title, the index bar and the glyph in three columns, so a finger can hit it anywhere along its length.

mark.why: The index bar is the one ink mark that sits beside an open title; it is empty while the section is closed so the titles never move.

label.why: The title prints at the reading size with a body-height line box, so wrapped lines and Thai marks keep room.

glyph.why: A dot-matrix plus while closed and minus while open is a second cue that does not rely on ink, at the end of the row where the thumb rests.

panel.why: The panel is a one-row grid whose row grows from zero to its content, so it opens to the exact height without a measured pixel value.

panelInner.why: The inner box clips the content while the row is shorter than the content, and without it the text would spill over the next section mid-travel.

body.why: The content stands under the title on the title's edge, indented past the index bar, so the section reads down one column.

hover.why: Hover only darkens a closed title's ink one step, because a real legend line does not rise when a hand comes near.

focus-visible.why: The focused header gets the 2px focus ring with an offset, so keyboard users always see which section the arrow keys will move from.

disabled.why: A header that cannot be pressed fades to the disabled opacity and shows the not-allowed cursor, and the native button leaves the tab order.

aria-expanded=true.why: An open title steps to primary ink and medium weight and its index bar fills, so the lit section is told by shape and weight as well as ink.

data-state=closing.why: A closing panel shrinks its row to zero and fades on motion.exit before it unmounts, so the content leaves instead of vanishing in one frame.

data-fresh=true.why: A section opened after the first render starts from a closed row and grows; one that was open at the start appears at once, so a page load stays still.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Nothing travels under Reduce motion: the row keeps its full height and the content only fades on the short hover timing.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the index bar is drawn in the button text colour and the seam stays a real border, so the lit section and the sections apart stay visible.

grid-template-rows.why: The row grows from zero on motion.enter and shrinks on motion.exit, fast in and slow out, with the content clipped while it travels.

opacity.why: The content fades in and out with the row on the same timing, so a closing panel does not show cut text at its shrinking edge.

color.why: The title's ink steps between secondary and primary on motion.hover, so the lit word changes without a jump.
